chapter: Cabarets and the Red Light District
title: Inside the Customs and Liberty cabaret and selling drinks
summary: Description of the cabaret, police detail, bandstand, tables, how short numbers made customers buy beer, and champagne prices.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: How big a place was that?
Well the cabaret, the cabaret then was about... It was just a little bit wider and the hangover club. Uh huh. See? And just about that long.
Was it a pretty rough place or was it...
Well it was a cabaret. You know what I'm gonna see? See them cabarets all had to have police detail there. If you just start off you'd go to jail there. Uh huh.
Was there a bandstand? Yeah, we had a bandstand.
The bandstand was about that high from the floor. About two or three feet? Three feet or so. Yeah, from the floor. Uh huh.

The tables all around. All around the wall. See? The tables all around over here. All around over here. All around over here. Up to the bandstand. See? The bandstand sit like out there. The tables like that door in there. Right? The bandstand. You know? Not too far.

The bandstand sit right there. They have to sit. Little step. See the girls. We'll catch them crowded houses. You don't play a full number. Cut that number off short. You'll get that float dancing. Cause it'll make them guys buy a lot of drinks. The shorter you cut that number the more drinks they buy. Cause every time you play. See? You can buy a bottle of beer. We start. As soon as you put that bottle of beer on the table. You take a swallow. See, you can buy a bottle of beer. We start up, as soon as you put that bottle of beer on the table, you take a swallow. If you don't take a swallow of that beer, when you come back from dancing with the girl, you'll buy another bottle of beer, and after that beer, that bottle is gone. Somebody just take it away? The waiter. Waiter, see. And if you're kind of a brosy guy, every time the girl stops dancing, you got a new waiter. Same way. I didn't wait on you. I had never seen you before, see. So you had to have a beer or dance. Yeah, you better drink some of that beer. Now champagne, the little bottles, you know the little bottle of champagne? That was set in the fire, Stance. And the big ones, your best champagne was a dollar and a half. Now you could go to a dance, go to a cafe, get laid, eat, dance all night, buy champagne, still come back home with some change. We did five. Because you could get the best, the cream of the crop, put away for a buck, and it wasn't one dollar.
That was the finest, 50 cents. All right. But you could tip, you know, there's no style of tipping, see. Yeah.
